title: Operator overloading

youtube.title: C++ Operator Overloading: + and << for Your Class | C++ Programming EP 59
youtube.description: In this episode you will overload plus for a class, overload the output operator and keep operators natural, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Operator overloading · 1:14 Add two points · 2:09 What the compiler calls · 2:57 Second program · 4:20 Recap · 4:50 Bug of the Day · 5:42 Challenge · 6:06 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "OPERATORS" in tomato on peach; Xecxec next to a plus sign wearing a class badge; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a plus sign wearing a class badge

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we teach operators new tricks. With your own plus, you can add two points as easily as two numbers.

scenes.onScreen: "Operator overloading": numbered lines (1. An operator is a function with a special name; 2. Plus for a class is operator plus; 3. Output uses operator with two arrows) and an analogy card: a language: the word add means something different for numbers and for fractions
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: An operator is a function with a special name. The plus operator for your class is a function called operator plus. When you write a plus b, the compiler calls it. The output operator is a free function that takes a stream and your object. Keep operators natural. Plus should add, and not delete files. When you overload an operator, you teach the language how your type behaves. A Vec class can add, subtract and print, like a number. Use this power with care. An operator should do what readers expect. If plus subtracts, your code is a puzzle for everyone.
points: An operator is a function with a special name
Plus for a class is operator plus
Output uses operator with two arrows

analogy.title: Operator overloading
analogy.body: A language: the word add means something different for numbers and for fractions

scenes.onScreen: vec.cpp: operator plus adds two Vec objects
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 6] The function name is operator plus. It takes another Vec by const reference. [HL 7] It returns a new Vec with the sums of the parts. [HL 12] A is one, two. [HL 13] B is ten, twenty. [HL 14] The compiler turns this into a dot operator plus of b. [HL 15] C is eleven, twenty-two. [HL 6] The function is named operator plus. It takes another Vec by const reference. [HL 7] It adds the two x values and the two y values, and it returns a new Vec. [HL 14] The compiler turns a plus b into a call to this function. [HL 15] The result is eleven and twenty-two.

scenes.onScreen: a table: the expression and the call behind it
scenes.animation: Table rows slide in one by one; the row the narrator mentions glows butter
scenes.narration: The table shows what happens. A plus b becomes a call to a dot operator plus, with b. Cout arrows a becomes a call to a free function called operator with two arrows. The operators are only a nicer way to write function calls. Notice that the call a plus b is a short form. Behind the scenes, it is a call to a dot operator plus of b. Both forms mean the same thing. The short form is easier to read.

diagram.caption: a table: the expression and the call behind it

scenes.onScreen: print.cpp: operator<< prints a Vec with cout
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 8] The first parameter is the output stream. The second is the object. [HL 9] The function prints the parts, and returns the stream. This lets us chain more arrows. [HL 14] Now cout can print a Vec as easily as a number. The output is Point, three, four, in brackets. [HL 8] The output operator is a free function. The left side is the stream, and the right side is our object. [HL 9] It writes the parts to the stream, and it returns the stream. That return lets us chain more arrows. [HL 14] Now cout can print a Vec, as it prints an int.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as print dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints Point followed by three comma four in round brackets. Notice that the output looks like a normal point, in round brackets with a comma.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. An operator is a function with a special name. Two. Operator plus lets you add objects. Three. The output operator takes a stream and an object. Four. Keep the meaning natural. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: An operator is a function with a special name.
Operator plus lets you add objects.
The output operator takes a stream and an object.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: An operator that does not exist
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the g++ error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. We add two Vec objects, but there is no operator plus. The compiler says no match for operator plus, with the operand types. It does not know how to add two points. Write operator plus in the struct. The compiler knows how to add numbers, but it cannot guess what you mean by adding two Vec objects. So it complains. Write operator plus for the class, and the same line works.

scenes.onScreen: I overloaded plus so that it adds fish. Now my program is full of surplus.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: I overloaded plus so that it adds fish. Now my program is full of surplus.

scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Add operator minus to Vec. Subtract one point from another, and print the result. Hint: follow the pattern of plus, and use a minus sign in both lines of the body. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: the rule of three, five and zero. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Compiler output (exactly as g++ prints it):

vec.cpp: In function 'int main()':
vec.cpp:11:15: error: no match for 'operator+' (operand types are 'Vec' and 'Vec')
   11 |     Vec c = a + b;
      |             ~ ^ ~
      |             |   |
      |             Vec Vec
bug.why: The compiler does not know how to add two Vec objects, until you write operator plus for them.

challenge: Add operator minus to Vec. Subtract one point from another, and print the result. Hint: follow the pattern of plus, and use a minus sign in both lines of the body.
challengeAnswer: Write Vec operator minus with a const reference. Return x minus other x, and y minus other y.
